title: Identification of physicochemical properties of spike proteins across diverse host species of SARS-CoV-2
author: Yerukala Sathipati, Tsai, et al.

steps.title: Install software and verify hardware
steps.instruction: Install R (version 4.1.2) and RStudio, Perl, LIBSVM v3.20 (C++), and the SPIKES pipeline from https://github.com/mingjutsai/SPIKES; ensure at least ~4 GB free disk space, 8 GB RAM, and a 1.5 GHz quad‑core processor; run on Mac OS or Linux.

steps.title: Download spike protein sequences
steps.instruction: Obtain S‑protein FASTA files for human and animal host coronaviruses from GISAID and NCBI (example IDs listed in Table 1); the combined dataset is also provided at the GitHub link; refer to the linked description of FASTA format for guidance.

steps.title: Reduce sequence redundancy
steps.instruction: Upload the downloaded FASTA files to the CD‑HIT web server (Huang et al., 2010) and run redundancy/ambiguity reduction as recommended; note that processing time depends on data size and computer speed.

steps.title: Convert sequences to numerical features
steps.instruction: Transform the redundancy‑reduced FASTA sequences into a numerical dataset by extracting (a) physicochemical properties (PCPs) from the AAindex database, (b) amino‑acid compositions, (c) di‑peptide compositions, and (d) pseudo‑amino‑acid compositions.

steps.title: Scale features and split dataset
steps.instruction: Apply feature scaling to the numerical matrix, then partition the data into training and test subsets for model training and evaluation.

steps.title: Run SPIKES for feature selection
steps.instruction: Execute SPIKES to (a) select an informative subset of the 531 AAindex PCP features and (b) tune SVM parameters; the GA‑chromosome contains binary genes for feature selection plus two 4‑bit genes encoding C and γ; IBCGA searches solution set Xr (r = r_start … r_end) using an RBF kernel; the tuned prediction model is available at the provided link.

steps.title: Compile AAindex extraction program
steps.instruction: In a terminal run: > git clone https://github.com/mingjutsai/SPIKES ; > cd SPIKES ; > cd src/aaindex ; > make to build the executable that converts FASTA sequences into the 531‑dimensional AAindex feature vectors.

steps.title: Calculate amino‑acid composition differences
steps.instruction: Using Microsoft Excel or GraphPad Prism 9, (a) compute amino‑acid compositions for all human and animal S‑protein sequences with the supplied code, (b) subtract animal values from human values (Human(A) – Animal(A)) to obtain composition differences, (c) record the resulting differences as the expected outcome.

steps.title: Measure SPIKES‑identified distinguishing features
steps.instruction: Extract the features that SPIKES flagged as informative and compare their values between human and animal S‑proteins to assess amino‑acid preference differences.

steps.title: Explore mutations with GISAID dashboard
steps.instruction: Access the CoVsurver spike‑glycoprotein mutation surveillance dashboard on GISAID, log in, select EpiCoV > spike glycoprotein mutation surveillance, and examine reported mutations in variants of interest.

steps.title: Install UCSF Chimera
steps.instruction: Download UCSF Chimera from the provided URL, install it on the workstation, and verify that it runs correctly.

steps.title: Measure PCPs for human and animal spikes
steps.instruction: Using the SPIKES‑selected PCP set, compute the PCP values for the human‑derived spike (Spike‑H) and animal‑derived spike (Spike‑A) to compare property differences.

steps.title: Extract amino‑acid and di‑peptide features via R
steps.instruction: In RStudio load the seqinr library and run: > library(seqinr) > Human <- ... > NonHuman <- ... ; then extract AAC and DPC with: > AAC <- t(sapply(Human, extractAAC)) ; > DPC <- t(sapply(Human, extractDC)) ; repeat for NonHuman; note that AAC yields a 20‑element vector, DPC a 400‑element vector (AA, AC … YY), and PseAAC a 80‑element vector for hydrophilicity/hydrophobicity.

steps.title: Visualize spike structure in Chimera
steps.instruction: Download the S‑protein PDB file (e.g., 6VXX) from the Protein Data Bank, open it in Chimera via File > Open > 6VXX.pdb, and inspect amino‑acid preferences in α‑helices and β‑sheets.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis of PCPs
steps.instruction: For each PCP compute mean ± standard deviation across groups; apply Student’s t‑test (p < 0.05) to compare human versus animal groups; use the LIBSVM package (Chang & Lin, 2011) to classify spikes as human‑derived or animal‑derived; refer to the additional details link for full parameters.
